SGTF-split case counts for England, autumn 2020 to January 2021

Source: R/data.R
EnglandB117.Rd

Daily PCR case counts for England split by S-gene target failure (SGTF), the data behind Volz et al. (2021) 's estimate of the transmissibility advantage of SARS-CoV-2 lineage B.1.1.7.

EnglandB117

Format

A list with five elements:

data

A data frame of 5,880 rows: date, area, corrected_positive (non-B.1.1.7), corrected_negative (B.1.1.7) and epiweek, for 49 areas over 120 days (2020-09-26 to 2021-01-23).

pop

Populations for 42 of those areas. The remaining seven are NHS England regions – aggregates of the others – which the source does not size, so they cannot be used with epiinf(pop_adjust = TRUE).

iar

England-wide daily infection ascertainment rate.

iar_sd

Standard deviation of the ascertainment rate, used as the prior scale on the observation coefficient.

i2o

Infection-to-observation kernel. The observations are weekly case totals attached to a daily series, so a daily delay distribution is spread over seven offsets; it therefore sums to 7, not 1.

Details

Routine testing in England used a three-target assay. B.1.1.7 carries a deletion that makes the S-gene target fail while the other two still amplify, so SGTF acts as a proxy for the lineage without sequencing every sample. Each area-day therefore splits into S-gene negative (B.1.1.7) and S-gene positive (everything else) counts, already adjusted for testing effort by the original authors.

The counts are aggregates. The raw SGSS line-list behind them is disclosure-controlled – counts below five are suppressed at source – so the raw-to-aggregate step cannot be reproduced outside PHE. Regenerate the aggregates with data-raw/england-b117.R, which pulls them from mrc-ide/sarscov2-b.1.1.7 at tag v1.0 (MIT licensed).

References

Volz E, Mishra S, Chand M, Barrett JC, Johnson R, Geidelberg L, Hinsley WR, Laydon DJ, Dabrera G, O'Toole Á, Amato R, Ragonnet-Cronin M, Harrison I, Jackson B, Ariani CV, Boyd O, Loman NJ, McCrone JT, Gonçalves S, Jorgensen D, Myers R, Hill V, Jackson DK, Gaythorpe K, Groves N, Sillitoe J, Kwiatkowski DP, Flaxman S, Ratmann O, Bhatt S, Hopkins S, Gandy A, Rambaut A, Ferguson NM (2021). “Assessing transmissibility of SARS-CoV-2 lineage B.1.1.7 in England.” Nature, 593(7858), 266–269. doi:10.1038/s41586-021-03470-x .
